items.briefing:
Cloudflare and Microsoft have jointly dismantled a sophisticated phishing service called EvilTokens that was specifically targeting Australian organisations. The operation used AI to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA), meaning even staff with MFA enabled could have had their accounts compromised. Separately, new research reveals that only 4% of Australian organisations regularly test their response to AI-related cyber incidents — a concerning gap given how rapidly AI-powered threats are evolving.

These two stories together highlight a clear message: having security measures in place isn't enough if they aren't regularly tested. **Practical tip:** Check with your IT team whether your organisation has a tested plan for responding to phishing attacks, including those that can bypass MFA.

featured.title: Cloudflare & Microsoft disrupt EvilTokens phishing service
featured.summary: More than 12,000 inboxes were exposed as the kit used to bypass multi-factor authentication and sustain account access was taken offline.
